chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Asama, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The believer is not tested with anything more difficult for him than three characteristics from which he is deprived.' It was said, 'And what are they?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Equalizing in what is in his hand (generosity/spending), and fairness with himself (self-restraint), and remembering Allah frequently. Indeed, I do not mean (merely saying) 'Glory be to Allah' and 'Praise be to Allah' and 'There is no god but Allah', but rather remembering Allah when what is permissible comes to him, and remembering Allah when what is prohibited comes to him.'

key_terms.الْمُوَاسَاةُ: Equalizing or being generous with one's wealth/resources

ai.seo_question: What are the three difficult characteristics a believer is tested with according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights that the most arduous trials for a believer are generosity (*muwasat*), self-restraint (*insaf*), and constant God-consciousness (*dhikr*). He distinguishes true *dhikr* from mere formulaic recitation, defining it as the active awareness of God in both permissible (*halal*) and prohibited (*haram*) actions, a concept central to Shia ethical jurisprudence. This emphasizes that spiritual depth is measured by consistent mindfulness across all dimensions of life, not just ritual performance.

en.hubeali: Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Asama who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Believer is not Tested with anything more difficult upon him than three characteristics depriving him’. It was said, ‘And what are these?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The equalisation regarding what is in his hands, and the fairness from himself, and remembering Allah<sup>azwj</sup> a lot. But, I<sup>asws</sup> am not saying (that one should be saying), ‘Glory be to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and the Praise for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and there is no god except for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’, but remembering Allah<sup>azwj</sup> during what is Permissible for him, and remembering Allah<sup>azwj</sup> during what is Prohibited upon him’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ibn Mahbub has narrated from abu ‘Usamah who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘The believer is not tried with anything more difficult than three depriving things.’ It was asked, ‘What are they?’ The Imam said, ‘They are to cooperate with one who has an established relation with you with whatever financial means available, to yield to justice for people against one’s own soul and to speak of and remember Allah very often. I, however, do not mean thereby saying, ‘All glory belongs to Allah, all praise belongs to Allah, and no one deserves to be worshipped except Allah. Speaking of Allah, and remembering Him is to do so (remember Him) when facing something that He has made lawful or that He has prohibited.’”
